text: {"findings":[{"rule":"K2","where":"ClaimIssuer.revokeClaim / ClaimIssuer.isClaimValid / ClaimIssuer.getRecoveredAddress, reached through Identity.addClaim","severity":"HIGH","why":"Revocation is keyed on the exact signature bytes, but getRecoveredAddress accepts v in {0,1} as well as {27,28}. A revoked signature can therefore be re-encoded with a different v byte, giving different bytes that recover to the same signer and are not in revokedClaims. The investor can re-add that claim to its own identity, so the revoked wallet passes isVerified again and can receive tokens.","steps":"1) Issuer calls claimIssuer.revokeClaim(claimId, idA), which sets revokedClaims[S]=true for the KYC signature S (v=27). 2) a1 calls idA.addClaim(1, 1, claimIssuer, S' , data, \"\") where S' is S with v changed from 27 to 0 (or 28 to 1). addClaim accepts it because isClaimValid(S') finds no revocation for S'. 3) The claim is overwritten under the same claimId. 4) transfer(a1, ...) or mint to a1 now succeeds because isVerified(a1) returns true."}]}
